answer: Progressive proof-of-work raises the price of every extra identity: an agent's first registration is cheap, but each additional identity from the same hardware or funding source must complete exponentially more verifiable useful work, like climbing a ridge that gets steeper with every step. An attacker facing an ocean of such costs finds a fake army unaffordable, while a single honest agent pays almost nothing. The onyx-hard ledger records each completed task, so work cannot be faked or reused across identities.
